title: Unified Animal Rush navigation
body: Animal Rush now uses the same compact circular glass Home button as every other game instead of its separate text-style control. The shared component also keeps Home navigation styling, iPhone safe-area placement and touch behaviour consistent across practice and challenge games.

title: Fixed the account bubble inside Chat
body: The global account bubble and its menu now render in a body-level overlay with explicit iOS touch and stacking behaviour. Chat's full-screen blurred layer can no longer intercept the button or hide the opened menu, and selecting Profile or another account section correctly closes the conversation and opens that page.

title: Modernised Admin Games for iPhone
body: Rebuilt each Admin Games row as a responsive management card so titles and descriptions remain readable on narrow iPhone screens. Ordering, game identity and status chips now occupy a clean header, while Reset, Settings, Challenge, visibility and playability use a separate labelled action grid with safe-area spacing and an extra-small-screen layout.

title: Separated live games from Challenge games
body: Admin Games now shows and controls whether each compatible game is available in Challenges, separately from its Home visibility and playable status. Animal Rush is clearly marked Live only and no longer appears when personal Challenge mode is selected. Team challenge creation follows the same admin configuration while existing team challenges retain their already-selected games.

title: Aligned the Animal Rush cards with the die
body: Animal cards now switch from question marks to their animal faces at the exact shared reveal deadline instead of waiting for the next 50 ms clock update and then fading in. The confirmed-working cube animation is unchanged, and live rooms and computer matches use the same immediate reveal behaviour.

title: Restored the complete 10:30am Animal Rush die
body: The cube now uses the complete React and CSS animation lifecycle from the confirmed working 10:30am main build, including its animation-start state, keyframes, easing and synchronised timing offset. All experimental v157–v161 animation changes have been removed. Hard mode prevents the old answer flash by placing the shuffle cover before the untouched animation reaches its final face.

title: Removed the iOS-incompatible die offset
body: The cube now starts the known-good animation normally and uses the remaining shared roll time as its duration, matching the earlier working implementation. The later negative CSS animation offset—which Safari could interpret as an already-finished roll—has been removed. The die and cards still reveal together at the shared server timestamp.

title: Restored the known-good Animal Rush die
body: The cube animation has been restored to the original fast version that worked correctly on iPhones before the recent reveal fixes. The only added behaviour is a final-frame concealment: the completed target face remains invisible until the existing shared reveal makes the die and cards appear together.

title: Rebuilt the Animal Rush cube animation for iOS
body: The die now uses two short, continuous hardware-accelerated rotations instead of one large multi-axis transform that Safari could render slowly or unevenly. The roll stays fast and smooth while remaining aligned to the shared round clock, and the target animal still appears only when the cards reveal.

title: Restored the fast Animal Rush die roll
body: The Animal Rush die no longer relies on iOS animation events to uncover the spinning cube. Its visibility now follows the synchronised round phase directly, restoring a fast continuous roll on every phone while keeping the final animal hidden until the cards reveal at the same shared moment.

title: Removed Animal Rush reveal and message glitches
body: The animated die now finishes on a neutral hidden state and shows its target only at the same reveal moment as the animal cards, removing the brief animal–question mark–animal flash. Card taps now use one authoritative round outcome, showing only You won this round or You lost this round instead of overlapping touch and winner messages.

title: Fixed Animal Rush leave errors
body: Fixed an Animal Rush database error that could prevent a player from leaving or rejoining a live room after the hidden-player privacy update. The v156 migration now installs the required hidden-player helper independently, and v155 is self-contained for future deployments.

title: Completed hidden-player privacy
body: Administrator-hidden players now disappear from Player Stats and every community surface for all viewers, including administrators. Team rosters, invitations, challenge summaries, live Animal Rush data, chats and transfer pickers now apply the same rule. Hidden accounts remain available only in Admin Players so they can be shown or moderated later. Profile wording now also distinguishes the player-controlled Private profile setting from detailed stats sharing.

title: Added selectable Animal Rush colours
body: Animal Rush now lets players choose between One colour, where shape recognition keeps the match fair and challenging, and Animal colours, where each character has its own easier-to-spot palette. The choice is available before computer matches and in live-room lobbies; live hosts control it and the room synchronises the same palette to every phone. The die and cards always use the selected palette together, and new attempt history records the colour mode for future reaction-time comparisons.

title: Closed hidden-player presence and Zoom label gaps
body: Hidden players are now excluded from the social online list for everyone, including administrators, while remaining manageable inside Admin Players. Hiding somebody also clears their active presence immediately, with database policy enforcement preventing direct presence reads from bypassing the rule. Zoom’s home tile now displays its proper English or Slovak description instead of the untranslated game.zoom.desc key.

title: Made Animal Rush recognition fairer
body: The Easy, Standard and Hard selectors now use compact glass surfaces with translucent depth, reflected highlights and a clearer mint-glass selected state. All six animals now share one coordinated teal palette so players must recognise their shapes rather than follow distinctive colours. In Hard mode, the die stays neutral throughout the hidden reshuffle and reveals its animal at the exact same server-owned moment as the final card faces.

title: Added synchronised Animal Rush difficulty modes
body: Animal Rush now offers Easy, Standard and Hard modes for computer and live matches. Live rooms wait until every phone is clock-synchronised, then the server sends one shared target, card order and future roll, shuffle and reveal times to every device. Hard mode keeps the cards visible during the roll, hides and reshuffles them as the die lands, then reveals the same final layout everywhere. Animation catch-up keeps delayed phones aligned, and anonymous attempt history now records per-mode reaction and error data for later balancing.

title: Made Animal Rush reveals harder and join errors cleaner
body: The six animal cards now remain fully concealed while the die rolls, revealing only when the target animal is ready so players cannot pre-scan card positions. A room-not-found response now appears directly inside the Join button and clears when the code is edited instead of creating a separate error panel.

title: Separated the Animal Rush countdown and die roll
body: New matches now show a synchronised 3–2–1 start countdown first, then begin a fresh three-second animal die roll instead of rolling invisibly behind the countdown. The live-room Join button now contains the six-character code guidance and remains disabled until the code is complete, removing the separate validation alert.

title: Stopped the Animal Rush target label moving the board
body: The target animal name now uses a permanently reserved label slot in both bot and live matches. Revealing or hiding the name no longer changes the board height, so the six animal cards stay fixed under players' fingers in portrait and landscape.

title: Stabilised Animal Rush rounds
body: Round-winner and touch feedback now appear as floating overlays, so the board no longer jumps down and back up. Every new match also begins with a clear full-board 3–2–1 countdown before the first animal is revealed.

title: Made Reduced Motion visible in Animal Rush
body: Animal Rush now detects the iPhone Reduce Motion preference, explains the static-die behaviour before play, and shows a compact Motion reduced badge during bot and live rounds. The status updates immediately when the device setting changes.

title: Stopped the Animal Rush die revealing early
body: Fixed an iOS Reduce Motion issue that could show the final animal before the countdown finished. Reduced-motion phones now see a neutral question-mark die during the countdown and the correct animal only at reveal; a safe neutral orientation also protects browsers where the spin cannot run.

title: Gave Animal Rush a more expressive animal cast
body: Redrew all six Animal Rush characters as colourful, expressive vector illustrations inspired by the physical cards: monkey, snake, octopus, elephant, spider and lion. The new artwork stays crisp on the animated cube and game cards while retaining compatibility with existing live rooms.

title: Added a 3D animal die to Animal Rush
body: Animal Rush rounds now begin with a modern animated 3D die whose six faces carry the six animals. It spins through the countdown, settles on the selected animal, works in both live and bot matches, and respects reduced-motion preferences.

title: Kept Animal Rush results inside the landscape board
body: Compacted the between-round result message in Animal Rush landscape mode so the target animal and its name always remain inside the left panel on phone screens.

title: Redesigned Animal Rush landscape board
body: Redesigned the Animal Rush landscape screen after phone testing. The target now has a clear panel on the left, all six animal cards use one balanced horizontal row, score content avoids the account button, and the board stays locked to the visible Safari viewport without awkward scrolling or clipped controls.

title: Play Animal Rush in landscape
body: Animal Rush now has a dedicated phone-landscape layout for both live and computer matches. Scores stay across the top, the target and round result sit on the left, and all six animal cards remain reachable in a compact 3-by-2 grid on the right.

title: Animal Rush now follows your theme
body: Animal Rush now uses a bright glass-and-mint appearance when ImBored is set to Light, while retaining its graphite appearance in Dark mode. Cards, controls, room entry, player scores, results and error states all switch with the selected app theme.

title: Test Animal Rush against the computer
body: Added a solo computer opponent to Animal Rush so the complete game can be tested from one phone. Rush Bot uses natural reaction delays, occasionally makes a wrong choice, follows the same safety-card and elimination rules, and never awards points or changes public statistics.

title: Animal Rush live phone game
body: Added Animal Rush, a phone-only live reaction game for 2–6 players. Players join with a room code, race for the animal shown by the shared die, protect two safety cards and lose won cards after their protection is gone. First touches, penalties, elimination and winners are resolved centrally for consistent play across phones.

title: Invite friends by email and complete What’s New history
body: Any approved player can now invite somebody who does not yet use the app by entering their email address. What’s New syncing has also been repaired so newer product updates appear again.

title: UI polish, Zip clarity and chat resilience
body: Simplified Zip, improved checkpoint and path readability, softened the Hive palette, refreshed game controls and made chat opening more resilient.

title: Team Daily Challenge notifications
body: When a team member finishes a Daily Challenge, every other teammate now receives an unread chat notification encouraging them to play. The update remains available for offline teammates, appears in Chats like any other unread message, and is generated only once per completed challenge result.

title: Poking, feedback editing, hint clarity, and hidden-player privacy fixes
body: Fixed a chain where an admin-hidden player could still show up as "online" and pokeable — poking them was then silently blocked server-side with no feedback to the sender, which looked like poking was broken entirely. Feedback editing (and every other Feedback action) now surfaces a clear message if a save fails instead of quietly doing nothing. Tango's hint now shows which symbol (sun or moon) actually belongs in the highlighted cell. Geo's map no longer shows a stray focus-outline rectangle after tapping a region. Practice/Challenge mode now remembers your last choice across a refresh instead of reverting to your profile default every time. The "new feedback" balloon in the account menu is no longer near-transparent and hard to read on small screens. Also hardened the admin Games settings screen (including hint-cooldown values) to surface save failures instead of looking successful either way, and added a missing database policy that could silently block saving cooldown settings for a game.

title: Challenge/Practice visual parity, points-transfer notifications, and stability fixes
body: The Challenge weekly-calendar screen now sits inside the same rounded white panel used by the actual game screens, matching Practice mode's look and feel instead of floating loosely on the grey background. Receiving points now surfaces a notification: a badge appears under the account bubble and on the My progress menu item, and My Progress shows who sent you points and how many. Also added: an app-wide error boundary so a crash in one game no longer takes down the whole app, code-splitting so games and admin screens load on demand, a fix for corrupted-data crashes in feedback notifications, and restored pinch-to-zoom for accessibility. Also fixed the real cause of headings looking inconsistent between screens (e.g. Geo's heading on Challenge vs Practice): the Fredoka font was only ever loaded by whichever game/Home/Login screen happened to be mounted, so leaving it removed the font for every other screen (Challenge's weekly calendar, Progress, Teams, Stats, Feedback, admin screens, etc.), silently falling back to the browser default. The font is now loaded once, globally, in index.html.

title: Cleaner navigation, profiles and release notes
body: Fixed completed-feedback notification errors without requiring the user_seen_at column. Practice and Challenge switches now show the destination mode and share aligned navigation. What's New displays the current app version, hides hidden entries by default and removes Delete controls. My Profile now uses a compact modern avatar picker.

title: Smarter Geo hints, unique questions, Zip snake and admin soft delete
body: Geo hints can be used repeatedly, question repetition protection is stricter, and the repeated McMurdo item was removed. Zip now draws a colourful snake along the route. Tango reset keeps elapsed time. Admins can soft-delete and restore Feedback and What's New items.

title: Greenland and New Zealand map regions
body: Geo now renders Greenland and New Zealand as separate tappable map regions and includes dedicated questions for Nuuk, Aotearoa, the kiwi bird and other region-specific facts. They remain geographically associated with North America and Oceania in ordinary continent questions.

title: Geo and Mini Sudoku polish
body: Geo now uses fact-based questions only, removes polar and New Zealand-specific content, and has a cleaner compact map with improved land styling and touch feedback. Mini Sudoku Reset now clears only player-entered cells while preserving elapsed time, mistakes, hints and hint cooldown; New still starts a completely fresh puzzle.

title: Improved completed-game flow
body: After saving a difficulty rating, the completed-game panel now stays open. Players can choose View board when ready instead of being redirected automatically, while Play again remains available.

title: Points remain visible after completion
body: The temporary Points popup now hides without clearing the awarded result. Points remain visible on the completed game page beside the final rating, so players can still see what they earned after the popup disappears.

title: Points stay visible on solved card
body: The Points awarded for a completed puzzle now remain visible inside the solved result card after the temporary celebration disappears.

title: Rewards & Progression
body: Earn Points for completed games Daily streaks and levels Simple My Progress and rewards UI Player wishes and Point transfers Streak protection using Points Admin rules, rewards, redemptions and adjustments

title: Daily stats and privacy
body: Player rows on Stats can now be expanded to show results grouped by day, including time, mistakes and hints. Profiles now include a Show my stats to others setting. Stats privacy is enforced by Supabase RLS; private stats remain visible to their owner and administrators.

title: Hidden players are now fully hidden
body: Fixed player hiding so it applies to all user-owned activity, not only the profile card. Hidden players are now excluded from public statistics, leaderboards, online presence, teams, feedback, votes, reactions and pokes. Admins can still see everything.

title: Smooth end-of-game rating flow
body: Fixed the solved panel briefly showing Play again before the difficulty question loaded. It now shows a short finalising state and then displays the correct rating prompt without flickering between layouts.

title: Reliable What’s New reactions
body: Fixed thumbs-up and thumbs-down reactions reverting after selection by saving them through an atomic authenticated database function.

title: Accounts & sign-in
body: Email code sign-in, Google sign-in, and passkey support. No passwords, and no confusing magic links.

title: Stats tracking
body: Every solved puzzle records your time, mistakes, and hints used — see it all on the Stats page.

title: Teams
body: Create a team, join as many as you like, add other players, or leave any time. Private profiles can't be added by anyone but themselves.

title: Challenge mode
body: One attempt per puzzle per day, the exact same puzzle for everyone, locked to real calendar dates. Miss a day? You can still catch it up later — still just one shot.

title: Mood status
body: Set a short status next to your name, visible to everyone.

title: Post-puzzle difficulty rating
body: Tap a bar right after solving to say how hard it felt. See the group's average difficulty before you even start a puzzle.

title: Feedback board
body: Suggest ideas, upvote other people's. Admin can mark things done with a comment.

title: Who's online
body: See who else currently has the app open and what they're playing. Tap someone to send them a fun poke.

title: Renamed to I'mBoredToday
body: New name, new playful font across the whole app.

title: Fixed mistake counting in Tango
body: Mistakes now only count when Hint actually catches something wrong — not on every tap. Matches how Hive already worked.

title: Nicer button hover/press effects
body: Every nav icon now has a springy lift on hover and a satisfying press on tap, each in its own accent color.

title: Difficulty rating redesigned
body: Switched from a tap-anywhere triangle to discrete tappable bars, matching watchOS's effort rating pattern.

title: Feedback form simplified
body: Down to a single text box instead of separate title and description fields.

title: Admin: hide a player
body: Admin can make a player invisible to everyone but themselves, enforced by the database itself, not just the UI.

title: Online widget redesign
body: Moved next to your profile, wiggles when others are online, expands into a list you can tap to poke someone.

title: Nav menu collapsed into one button
body: Profile, Feedback, Stats, Teams, and Sign out now live behind a single avatar button instead of cluttering the top bar.

title: Fixed missing Home buttons
body: Teams, Stats, Feedback, Profile, and the Challenge screen all had a barely-visible back arrow — replaced with a clear, labeled Home button everywhere.

title: Feedback notification badge
body: The nav button now wiggles with a purple count badge whenever there's open feedback waiting to be reviewed.

title: Fixed online status
body: You now show as online for the whole time the app is open, not just while mid-puzzle.

title: Fixed a login-breaking bug
body: A database policy had an infinite recursion bug that could block sign-in entirely. Fixed at the database level.

title: This page
body: Release notes are now fully automatic, synced from a changelog file on every deploy — nobody types these in by hand.

title: Release notes cleanup
body: Removed manual post/delete controls (the changelog file is the single source of truth now) and added version numbers to every entry.

title: Stats split by Challenge/Practice
body: Toggle between the two — practice is unlimited so its counts aren't really comparable, challenge is the fair one-shot-a-day metric. Each game shown separately, plus a total.

title: Fixed the mystery hide button
body: Admin's player-hide toggle only had a hover tooltip, which does nothing on a phone. Now has a visible text label.

title: Fixed release notes not updating
body: The sync used 'ignore-duplicates', which skips any entry that already exists instead of updating it. Switched to 'merge-duplicates' so edits to CHANGELOG.json actually take effect on already-synced entries.

title: Fixed missing Home button on the Solved! screen
body: The post-puzzle rating screen (challenge and practice mode both) had no way back to Home at all — only its own continue button. Added a back arrow, top-left.

title: New game: Mini Sudoku
body: 6x6 sudoku, verified unique every time, difficulty scales through the week via clue count. Hint uses real solving techniques (naked/hidden singles, contradiction test) — never a guess. Works in both Challenge and Practice mode, same as the others. Also brought Hive/Tango/Zip's fonts in line with the rest of the app.

title: New admin screen: Players
body: Lists every signed-up player, not just ones who've played something (unlike Stats' hide toggle, which only shows players with game history). Admin-only, hide/unhide from here.

title: Mini Sudoku redesigned
body: White cells throughout, bold black for given numbers vs. light gray for your own entries (not blue), a green outline for the selected cell instead of a filled tint, and a proper 4-column number pad with Erase and Undo built right in.

title: Mode indicator while playing
body: A Challenge/Practice pill now shows the whole time you're playing, and tapping it switches modes without backing out to Home first.

title: Cleaned up the online widget
body: No longer shows "1 online" when that one person is just you.

title: Last seen tracking
body: The admin Players screen now shows when each player was last active, not just whether they're online right now.

title: Best times leaderboard
body: Expanding a completed challenge day now shows the fastest 5 times for that specific day.

title: Added a favicon
body: The browser tab now shows an actual icon instead of a blank one.

title: New admin screen: Games
body: Control which games show on the home screen, whether they're playable or "coming soon", and their display order.

title: Choose your default mode
body: New setting on the Profile screen: pick whether you land in Challenge or Practice mode after logging in.

title: Fixed a gap in the new Games admin screen
body: It didn't check admin status internally — the database would've blocked a non-admin from actually saving changes, but the screen would misleadingly let them try. Fixed.

title: Fixed Hive sometimes requiring a guess
body: Found the real cause: some puzzles needed a brute-force deduction technique that's essentially unspottable by eye. Generation now rejects any layout that ever needs it — every hint step is now something a person could actually reason out, verified across dozens of test puzzles at every size.

title: Played-today badge on Home
body: See at a glance which games you've already completed today's challenge for, without opening each one.

title: Reset now counts as a mistake in Hive
body: Starting over after making progress counts against you, same spirit as everything else.

title: Hint cooldown, admin-configurable
body: Admin can set how long Hint locks after each use, per game, with an optional per-day ramp so it can get stricter as difficulty increases through the week. Off by default everywhere.

title: Sudoku flashes a completed section
body: Finish a row, column, or box correctly and it briefly pulses, not just the final win.

title: Fixed hidden games flashing visible
body: A hidden game would show briefly on every page load before disappearing. The config was loading async and defaulting to "show everything" in the meantime — now waits for the real answer first.

title: Rating moved onto the game screen
body: No more jumping to a separate page after solving — the difficulty rating now appears right on the completed board. Challenge mode hides "Play again" since it's one attempt only; your result stays visible on the challenge screen's day list any time.

title: Fixed What's New showing entries out of order
body: The sort relied on a timestamp that got recomputed differently every time the sync ran, so entries pushed at different times could interleave wrong. Now sorts by version number, which is fixed and never changes, and switched dates to a fixed value too so they stop drifting.

title: Thumbs up/down on What's New
body: React to any update — thumbs up if it's working, thumbs down if it's not. A thumbs-down automatically creates an entry on the Feedback board (with an optional note about what went wrong), so it's actually followed up on, not just a silent downvote.

title: Fixed Undo/Reset working after solving
body: Undo and Reset stayed clickable even after a puzzle was solved. Undoing the winning move and re-entering it triggered a second save attempt, which hit the once-a-day database limit and kicked you to "already completed" with no explanation. Both are now locked the moment a puzzle is solved, across all four games.

title: Difficulty rating collapses after you pick
body: Instead of staying open, it now shrinks to a small confirmation pill so the completed board underneath gets the space back.

title: Gameplay fixes across all puzzle modes
body: Difficulty rating now closes the solved overlay and leaves a compact rating indicator on the read-only board. Mini Sudoku hints reveal the correct number, incorrect entries increment mistakes immediately, hint cooldowns resist rapid repeated clicks, and dashboard activity is separated between Challenge and Practice.

title: Admin: reset today's challenge
body: Admins can reset today's saved challenge results for an individual game from the Games admin screen, allowing everyone to replay that day's challenge.

title: Release notes workflow repaired
body: Updated checkout to the Node.js 24-compatible action, added clear secret and changelog validation, and made Supabase errors visible in GitHub Actions instead of failing without a useful response body.

title: Clearer difficulty rating feedback
body: After choosing a difficulty, the solved panel now briefly confirms that the rating was saved before returning to the board. The saved rating is shown as a compact six-bar indicator matching the original picker, with the selected level highlighted.

title: Clearer reactions on What's New
body: Thumbs up and thumbs down now always show their counts and update immediately. Your selected reaction changes colour, tapping it again removes it, and choosing the opposite reaction switches your vote instead of allowing both.

title: What's New reactions now persist
body: Fixed release-note reactions reverting immediately after selection by using explicit insert, update and delete operations instead of an RLS-sensitive upsert.

title: Admins can hide What's New entries
body: Admins can now hide or show individual What's New entries. Hidden updates remain visible to admins with a clear badge, are excluded for ordinary players, and retain their existing reaction counts.

title: Points, streaks & levels
body: Every solve earns points based on speed, mistakes, and hints — build a daily streak, level up over time, and spend points in the new Rewards shop (admin-approved redemptions, plus a wishlist and player-to-player transfers).

title: New admin screen: Rewards
body: Tune the points formula, manage the rewards catalog, review wishlist and redemption requests, and manually adjust a player's balance.

title: Hidden-player privacy, properly complete
body: The earlier hide feature only hid the profile row itself. Now a hidden player's stats, leaderboard entries, presence, team memberships, feedback, votes, and pokes are all hidden at the database level too.

title: Fixed hint cooldown not taking effect
body: Game settings only loaded once when the app first opened, so changing the hint cooldown mid-session wouldn't reach an already-open game without a full reload. Now refetches the moment you enter a game.

title: New game: Geo
body: Five geography questions a day — a simplified world map plus capitals, landmarks, and native wildlife by continent. Difficulty ramps through the week from famous/easy to properly obscure. 50/50 hint available, same cooldown system as the other games.

title: Fixed a blank-page crash
body: A missing icon import in Stats.jsx crashed the entire app before anything could render, including login. This time verified by actually running the built app in a real browser and checking for errors, not just a successful build.

title: Fixed Geo's map — it was genuinely bad
body: The first version was built blind, without ever actually seeing it rendered, and it showed — unrecognizable blob shapes. Rebuilt with real visual verification this time (actual screenshots checked at each step, not guessed coordinates), so the continents now read clearly and are properly proportioned.

title: Geo's map now uses real geographic data
body: Replaced the hand-drawn continent shapes with ones traced from actual Natural Earth coastline data, simplified down cleanly. Should read as real continents now, not abstract blobs.

title: Added New Zealand, Greenland, Madagascar & Antarctica to Geo's map
body: The first real-data pass only kept the single largest landmass per continent, silently dropping genuinely significant secondary ones. Now keeps any landmass at least 1.5% of the mainland's size, plus a simple decorative Antarctica band so the map doesn't look cropped.

title: Geo's question pool nearly tripled
body: Added 118 countries (deliberately excluding every transcontinental/contested case — Russia, Turkey, Kazakhstan, the Caucasus, Cyprus — so nothing is debatable), bringing the total pool from ~60 facts to 177. Static data, no external API dependency, and this scale should hold up to daily play for a long time before repetition becomes noticeable.

title: Closed a real points exploit in team challenges
body: Any team owner could set a weekly team challenge's reward up to 100,000 points, credited straight to their real balance on completion — with no relation to normal scoring. That reward is now capped at 500 (enforced in three independent places), and existing challenges above that are clamped down automatically. No action needed.

title: Points economy hardened against misconfiguration
body: The admin-tunable scoring rules had no upper bound, so a stray extra zero would have applied to every game, for everyone, instantly. Every scoring field now has sane limits, and point awards are clamped to an absolute ceiling independent of those settings. Normal play is unaffected — every default was already well inside the new limits.

title: Geo's world got a second layer: subregions
body: All 117 countries now carry a subregion (Southern Europe, South-eastern Asia, Andean South America, and so on) between continent and country. This is the data layer the new Zoom game drills through — continent, then region, then country — and it's available for future geography features too.

title: New game: Zoom
body: Three rounds, three quick two-option questions each — continent, then region, then country — all following one clue (an animal, a landmark, a flag) all the way down to the answer. Same daily-challenge structure as the other games, same scoring pipeline, no separate points system.

title: Zoom: clearer controls, flora questions, easier recall
body: Removed the toolbar's redundant ‘New’ button (Restart already covers it). Answer buttons now sit side by side. The continent/region breadcrumb now reveals what was actually correct at each step you've passed, so reaching the country question doesn't require remembering the continent/region cold. Also added flora questions (24 countries) alongside the existing animal/landmark/food/currency/language/flag clues.

title: Unified game toolbars, fixed a misleading icon
body: Geo had the same broken 'New' button Zoom had (a no-op mid-quiz) — removed, folded into Restart. The Eraser icon on Geo and Zoom's restart button was misleading (nothing is being erased, a fresh quiz is generated) — swapped for a refresh icon. Disabled toolbar buttons (Undo before your first move, Hint on cooldown, etc.) were low-contrast enough to read as missing rather than temporarily unavailable — bumped visibility across every game. Removed a small, unexplained icon that appeared under Zoom's flag prompts.

title: Home screen: smaller header, straight to the games
body: The giant centered app-name heading is gone, replaced with a compact header row like the games hubs this app is modeled on (NYT Games, LinkedIn Games). Points and streak moved into a small chip instead of a separate big card. Games start noticeably higher on the screen — nothing about what the page does changed, just how much space it took to get there.

title: Game polish: bigger grids, thicker walls, gloss effects, smarter errors
body: Zip: 6x6 → 7x7 grid for more substance; walls thicker (3px → 5px). Hive: board border-radius reduced from rounded-xl to rounded-lg, less cartoonish. Tango: sun/moon icons 40% bigger; constraint symbols (=/×) bigger and in larger containers; sun now fully filled instead of outline. Home: practice/challenge toggle now has a gloss effect with gradient overlay and enhanced shadows. Tango validation: errors no longer show instantly while typing — now debounced to 2 seconds, only shown after the full pause (not during continuous editing). Fixed race condition in practice-mode checkboxes that showed incomplete state before data finished loading.

title: Game fixes: Zip difficulty scaling, Tango smart delays, gloss effects, green dot bug, no more holes
body: Zip: checkpoint numbers now scale Monday (4) → Sunday (16); walls increase 0→7; black holes removed entirely (visual & gameplay); tunnels capped at 1; grid size 7×7. Tango: conflict errors now debounced to 2 seconds but clear instantly (no delayed clearing). Hive: board border-radius refined. App: iOS-style gloss effect applied globally via new .gloss-button class; Home toggle now uses it. Home: fixed race condition in practice-mode checkmarks — only show after data loads. Presence: immediately clears when exiting a game (was delayed up to 45s, caused 'playing' indicator to persist).

title: Complete feedback implementation: Text-only game buttons, immediate Tango errors, gloss CSS foundation, Zip tuning
body: Game Toolbars: Converted all 6 games from icon-only to TEXT LABELS spread evenly across top edge (Undo/Reset/New/Hint or Restart/Hint). Clean typography, mobile-friendly. Tango: Constraint violations (sun+sun with =) now show red IMMEDIATELY with no delay. Zip: Checkpoints scale 4→16 (Mon-Sun); walls 0→7; tunnels max 1; removed all black hole visuals; grid 7×7 with 5px walls. Presence: Fixed 45s delay bug — leaving a game now clears the green 'playing' indicator immediately.
